intelligence.human_view: This is the finish-what-you-start law applied to the page that matters most. Personal is the first world — the citizen's own — and Business and Space are not new builds, they are clones of the finished Personal. That order is the whole point: if Personal is not finished, there is nothing to clone, and building Business and Space from an unfinished Personal just multiplies the unfinishedness by three. The Tetris composer is the proof of what "finished" means: not "mostly there" but one flush line, search and post and Smart note and Naya note lined up tight, looking pro — an item named on Nov 13, still owed on Nov 14, and named again because naming it once did not finish it. "You can look it up" is the giveaway: the correction was already written down, in the brief, as Part 6 / D10 — the failure was not that nobody knew, it was that knowing did not become doing. Finish means the page he sees is the page the brief describes, whole, and only then does the clone run.
intelligence.simple_view: First you finish your very own page — ALL the way finished, every piece perfect! THEN you copy it to make the Business page and the Space page — like photocopying your beautiful drawing! You don't start three drawings and finish none of them — you finish ONE, beautifully, and then you copy it!
intelligence.grandma_view: You finish the first one properly, love — all the way, every piece in its place, lined up neat as a pin. Then you copy it for the others, and they're just as beautiful. You don't start three things and finish none of them — you finish one, and then the rest follow, easy as pie.
intelligence.naya_view: I finish Personal for real, then I clone it to Business and Space. I am not done until he is not waiting on those edits anymore. The composer lines up on one flush bar — search and post and Smart note and Naya note, Tetris-tight, looking pro, the Live Feed label gone, buttons lit their own colors. I finish one page whole, and the clones follow from the finished page — identical except title and story, never rebuilt.
